title: Staff AI, Student Proof: The Integrity Divide Schools Must Name
content:
[Name], the most honest conversation in education forums this week is not about banning AI — it is about **who gets to use it**.

Teachers describe AI saving hours on worksheets, cover lessons, rubrics, and the paperwork principals suddenly want as evidence. Training programmes in larger colleges treat it as a supervised tool, not a shortcut around judgment.

In the same scroll, science and high-school threads move the opposite way: graded work stays in the classroom, notebooks become proof, and take-home polish is treated as a risk — not a virtue.

Students notice the gap. So do parents. PD that says "embrace the future" without naming **practice versus proof** is where trust breaks.

EduHexa works with 100+ institutions to align smart classrooms, assignment design, and parent language when leaders need **two clear lanes** — not one vague slogan.

Which lane is written down in your school today: staff AI rules, student proof rules, or neither?
excerpt: Teacher forums embrace AI for planning while student work shifts to in-class proof — schools need a published two-lane charter before the next integrity dispute.
